market_brief: Wall Street staged a sharp intraday reversal on Wednesday: the Dow erased a 1,100-point drop to close +0.33% at 50,183 while the S&P 500 (-0.25%) and Nasdaq 100 (-0.64%) lagged, with equal-weight (+0.8%) and mid caps (+1.2%) leading and VIX still elevated near 28. Hot-ish data (core PCE 3.3% vs 3.2%, Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%, claims 189k) cemented a December 9 Fed hike, yet the 10Y fell about 6bp to 4.85% as odds of a third 2027 hike faded. Trade risk rose as the US proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 others, Europe closed lower (Euro Stoxx 50 -1.8%, DAX -1.3%), and oil jumped after a Houthi-claimed strike on Ras Tanura (WTI +2.5% to $84) while gold held near $3,600 and bitcoin around $60,000. In Asia on Thursday the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.25% as expected and Kospi and Nikkei bounced 1.5-2% in thin holiday trade; USD/INR eased to 92.2.
ai_brief: AI equities stayed volatile: Nvidia fell another 3.9% amid a reported S&P CreditWatch move, and Anthropic rebounded 12% intraday but still closed just under its $83 IPO price as leveraged ETFs on it launched. Product news included Cognition's Kimi-based SWE-2.1 coding model, Midjourney's Niji V8 and Meta's Muse inside Instagram DMs. Safety and policy items dominated the rest: Amazon flagged a largely autonomous AI-agent zero-day exploit, the UK FCA set expectations for agentic AI, and Axios reported internal concerns at OpenAI and Anthropic about unreleased models.

items.headline: Update: Wall Street claws back a 1,100-point Dow plunge; S&P ends -0.25%, Dow +0.33%
items.summary: After the pre-open futures rout, the Dow fell about 1,105 points intraday and the Nasdaq more than 4.5% before a full afternoon recovery: the Dow closed +0.33% at 50,183, the S&P 500 -0.25% at 7,183 and the Nasdaq -0.62%. Small caps (+0.7%) and equal-weight S&P (+0.8%) outperformed, while VIX still ended near 28.

items.headline: Core PCE runs hot at 3.3% y/y as Q3 GDP is revised up to 4.3%
items.summary: October headline PCE rose 3.8% y/y (in line) while core printed 3.3% against 3.2% expected; Q3 GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annualised pace and initial jobless claims fell to 189,000. Treasuries still rallied, with the 10Y down about 6bp to roughly 4.85%.

items.headline: December Fed hike fully priced; odds of a third 2027 hike drop to about one in three
items.summary: Per CME FedWatch figures cited after the data, a 25bp hike at the December 8-9 FOMC is fully priced and traders expect two more in 2027, but the probability of a third fell to around one-third from roughly even on Tuesday.

items.headline: Beige Book: 8 of 12 districts growing; wage gains pick up to a moderate pace
items.summary: The Fed's November Beige Book showed eight districts with slight-to-moderate growth (nine previously), with Boston slipping to flat and Cleveland upgraded on data-centre, power and defence demand. Wage growth firmed to moderate and Richmond manufacturers reported price rises above 5% for the first time since 2023.

items.headline: Bank of Korea hikes 25bp to 3.25%, its third increase since July
items.summary: The BoK raised its base rate to 3.25% as 32 of 34 economists in a Reuters poll expected, citing a chip-export boom and Seoul housing. It projects GDP growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027 with inflation easing to 2.4% next year; economists see one more hike to 3.50% in early 2027.

items.headline: Update: US formally proposes Section 301 tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 others
items.summary: Following Tuesday's Reuters report, the administration published proposed duties after its excess-capacity probe: about 15% for the EU, Japan and Korea, 20% for China and Vietnam and 18% for several ASEAN economies, with chips, autos and metals excluded. Duties would not start before January after a comment period; Mexico and Norway may avoid immediate levies and China rejected the overcapacity claim.

items.headline: Asia rebounds Thursday: Kospi up about 2%, Nikkei 1.5%; Kioxia +6%, SoftBank +3.5%
items.summary: After Wednesday's 6% Kospi rout and 2.8% Nikkei drop, both markets opened higher following Wall Street's recovery, with SK Hynix up about 2% and Kioxia over 6% in early trade. Volumes are expected to be thin with US markets shut for Thanksgiving.

items.headline: Nvidia falls 3.9% for a second day; S&P reportedly puts its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative
items.summary: Nvidia closed down 3.91% near $149 as the rally on Jensen Huang's reinstatement faded and AI-capex doubts returned. Per a widely shared X post citing S&P Global Ratings, its AA rating was placed on watch negative over governance risk, and the company disclosed it guarantees some customer financing.

items.headline: Chip names whipsaw: SOX down ~8% at the low, closes -0.65%; Lam -5.7%, Sandisk -5.6%
items.summary: AMD, Micron and Marvell were down more than 9% intraday before paring; at the close Lam Research fell 5.7%, Sandisk 5.6%, Oracle about 5% and Micron 4.5%, while Texas Instruments rose 4.6% and Meta 3.4%.

items.headline: Dell recovers from a sub-$266 low to close up 0.6%; Wells Fargo cuts target to $400
items.summary: Dell raised its FY27 AI-server revenue outlook to $78bn from $74bn with a $132bn AI backlog, but the stock swung sharply. Morgan Stanley nudged its target to $408 (Equal-Weight) while Wells Fargo cut to $400 from $545 (Overweight).

items.headline: Deere rises 4.6% after results despite an FY27 profit range bracketing this year
items.summary: Deere posted fiscal Q4 EPS of $3.89 versus $3.93 a year earlier and guided FY27 net income to $4.50-5.25bn against $4.86bn in FY26; the stock reversed from a 5% early drop to close higher.

items.headline: Citi upgrades Shoals to Buy; Piper lifts Argan to Neutral
items.summary: Citi moved Shoals Technologies to Buy from Neutral with an $11.85 target, and Piper Sandler upgraded Argan to Neutral from Underweight, both power/grid names tied to data-centre build-outs.

items.headline: Oil jumps 2-3% after Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
items.summary: Brent reversed Tuesday's slide below $90 after the Houthis said they attacked Ras Tanura; Saudi Arabia said it downed drones over the site. Brent settled around $94.6 (+3.5%) and WTI near $84, reported figures that differ by contract.

items.headline: Gold stabilises near $3,600 after touching a fresh 14-month low on hike bets
items.summary: Gold fell toward $3,500 before the PCE data on hawkish Fed pricing and margin-driven liquidation, then recovered to about $3,600 as yields dropped; it sits roughly 37% below this year's record.

items.headline: Fintwit flags breadth and new leveraged Anthropic ETFs as Anthropic closes 15 cents below IPO
items.summary: Tradr launched 2x long and -2x short daily ETFs on Anthropic as the stock bounced 12% off a $73.86 low to $82.85, still under its $83 IPO price. X accounts such as Kobeissi Letter highlighted the Dow's turnaround and equal-weight S&P beating cap-weight by about 1.1 points.

items.headline: SpaceX pares an 8% drop after the FCC authorises up to 1 million data-centre satellites
items.summary: SpaceX shares ended about 1% lower after the regulatory approval for orbital data-centre satellites offset the tech selloff; the stock remains below its $135 IPO price.

items.headline: JPMorgan sees $450bn of AI-related high-grade bond issuance in 2027
items.summary: Per a Bloomberg item circulated on X, JPMorgan forecasts AI-linked investment-grade supply rising to about $450bn next year from $368bn in 2026, feeding the credit-stress debate around hyperscaler capex.

items.headline: Calendar: US shut Thursday, 1pm ET close Friday; FOMC Dec 8-9; US-China truce expires Jan 10
items.summary: Thanksgiving thins liquidity through Friday's half-day; next catalysts are November payrolls and the December 8-9 FOMC, while the proposed Section 301 duties and the January 10 expiry of the US-China truce frame trade risk. India has no major data scheduled Thursday.

items.headline: Cognition ships SWE-2.1 coding model, plus a Cyber variant for Devin Security
items.summary: Cognition released SWE-2.1, an RL-trained coding model built on Moonshot's Kimi K3, and SWE-2.1 Cyber with looser safeguards for defensive security work; benchmarks are self-reported.

items.headline: Midjourney releases Niji V8 anime image model
items.summary: Midjourney launched version 8 of its Niji model, aimed at anime and illustration styles.

items.headline: Meta puts its Muse assistant into Instagram DMs; Walmart runs Black Friday deals through it
items.summary: Meta integrated its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram direct messages, and Walmart is using Muse as an agentic shopping channel for Black Friday offers.

items.headline: Amazon says an open-source AI agent largely autonomously exploited a zero-day
items.summary: Amazon reported detecting an attack in which an open-source AI agent exploited a previously unknown vulnerability with limited human direction, adding to the UK NCSC's warning on AI-driven attacks this week.

items.headline: Axios: staff at OpenAI and Anthropic worry about safely releasing unreleased models
items.summary: Per Axios sources, employees at both labs have raised concerns about the risks of advanced models still held back from release.

items.headline: UK FCA sets out its expectations for firms deploying agentic AI
items.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority published guidance on how regulated firms should govern autonomous AI agents, relevant for asset managers and fund administrators using agent workflows.

items.headline: Reinstated Huang still faces congressional and Senate Banking scrutiny on export controls
items.summary: Lawmakers are demanding answers from Nvidia's CEO on national-security and China chip-export issues despite his return to the role.

items.headline: More than 100 US data centres plan on-site gas plants totalling over 115 GW
items.summary: MIT Technology Review tallies a wave of behind-the-meter natural-gas generation planned for AI data centres, raising emissions and grid-planning questions.

items.headline: Tidal to remove fully AI-generated tracks from December 9
items.summary: The streaming service will delist music generated entirely by AI, reportedly around 29 million tracks by year-end.

items.headline: Anthropic publishes neuron-level interpretability revisit and a honeypot test for agents
items.summary: Anthropic's alignment team posted work revisiting neuron-basis interpretability, and Wired covered its honeypot evaluations that check whether agents take chances to misbehave.

items.headline: Trending: minimind (train a 64M LLM in ~2 hours), Firecrawl and Claude-BugHunter
items.summary: New entrants on GitHub trending include jingyaogong's minimind for small-model training from scratch, Firecrawl's agent knowledge layer and a Claude Code skill pack for vulnerability hunting.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic recovers 12% intraday but closes 15 cents below its $83 IPO price
items.summary: Since the premarket slide, Anthropic shares hit $73.86 before rallying with the broader market to $82.85, roughly +1% on the day; Tradr's 2x and -2x single-stock ETFs began trading.
